description: Rotavise is a team taking on the Field Shift challenge. We’ll build a web app that combines NASA weather history, soil information and crop requirements to help farmers plan what to grow across seasons, with clear reasons for each recommendation. I’m Houdaifa Drahm a backend and DevOps engineer, I’ll handle the backend and deployment. We’re looking for teammates in frontend development, UX, agriculture.
summary: Rotavise is an open-source prototype that helps Moroccan farmers explore crop rotations using NASA environmental data, local soil context, crop characteristics and farmer priorities. The backend compares multi-year sequences and reports evidence, risks and missing information rather than promising a single perfect crop. NASA POWER supplies historical weather, and NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 supports comparisons across future climate scenarios. Our interface includes a satellite map, field tools, a multilingual crop catalog and a glossary; several results screens remain unfinished. We provide the public source code and a slide demonstration of the implemented components. Rotavise supports discussion with farmers and agronomists, not a replacement for their judgment. Crop rules need expert review, and model outputs are not validated farm yield forecasts.
details:
Rotavise is an open-source decision-support prototype for the Field Shift challenge, focused on Moroccan farming conditions. It helps explore multi-year crop sequences using environmental evidence and farmer priorities. It supports local agricultural judgment rather than replacing it.

HOW IT WORKS

A farmer identifies a field, records crop history and chooses a planning horizon and priorities. The backend uses a versioned crop catalog and deterministic bounded search to compare sequences, with evidence coverage, risks and missing information. NASA POWER provides historical weather. NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 provides future-climate comparisons across multiple models and two emissions pathways. Other implemented adapters include GPM rainfall, soil and satellite context, with availability depending on configuration. Dataset values represent grid areas rather than on-field sensors.

CURRENT PROTOTYPE

The locally running interface includes a satellite map, saved fields, a multi-step rotation builder, crop catalog and glossary, with English and French interface support. A demonstration field was saved through the real API during submission preparation. The backend reports complete prepared climate coverage for its 89 configured positions. Several results, evidence and secondary frontend screens are unfinished. There is no public live deployment. The repository is the final project artifact; the demonstration uses actual local screenshots and clearly labelled historical backend evidence. The photo-check feature is disabled in this installation because an AI key is not configured.

TECHNOLOGY AND ORIGINALITY

The project uses TypeScript, React, Vite, MapLibre, a Node.js API and worker, PostgreSQL, shared Zod contracts and an optional Python science service. Versioned requests, catalog releases and provenance support reproducibility. Its intended contribution is to connect rotation choices with climate evidence, uncertainty and local crop knowledge in a workflow farmers can discuss with advisers.

LIMITATIONS AND NEXT STEPS

Crop rules are not expert reviewed. Some catalog facts originate from AI model recall and carry that provenance. Water, carbon and yield models require local calibration. Comparisons are exploratory, not validated yield or income forecasts. The search is bounded, and missing evidence must not be interpreted as suitability. Next steps are completing the results interface, testing with Moroccan farmers and agronomists, and validating model performance before deployment.

AI DISCLOSURE

Claude and Codex assisted coding, debugging, research, documentation, translation and presentation preparation under team direction. Some crop facts come from model recall and remain unverified. Optional AI explanation and photo-check integrations exist but are not claimed as live demonstrated features. The rotation-ranking engine is deterministic. Screenshots show the actual application, not generated product mockups.

DEVELOPMENT HISTORY

Development began on September 26, 2026, before the November 14-15 event. This submission includes pre-existing work. Organizer approval for award eligibility has not been verified; we disclose this for organizer review. The repository preserves the project history.

REFERENCES

Full dataset and research references, usage notes and known licensing gaps are documented in docs/REFERENCES.md. Software dependencies and licenses are listed in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. The project is licensed Apache-2.0.
